subject: Urban Planning
title: Detroit: Planning for Shrinkage
description: A quick, practical guide to Detroit: Planning for Shrinkage.

hook.text: Detroit went from 1.8 million people in 1950 to 640,000 today. What do you plan for when a city shrinks?

buildup.text: Entire neighborhoods emptied. 78,000 buildings were abandoned. Streetlights served nobody.

discovery.text: The city began 'rightsizing' — demolishing empty blocks and converting them to urban farms and forests.

twist.text: Some residents refused to move from scattered blocks, forcing the city to maintain services for a few houses.

climax.text: Detroit's approach is now studied worldwide. Dozens of shrinking cities face the same challenge.

punchline.text: Planning usually means growth. Detroit had to plan for the opposite.

quiz.question: What is 'rightsizing' in urban planning?
options: Increasing building heights to match population growth
Shrinking city infrastructure to match a declining population
Standardizing lot sizes across different neighborhoods
